account:
Today has mostly followed ordinary town business: market visits, accounts at the office, and tea with my neighbour at the cottage near the east ferry landing. The unusual item is a vague mention of a bridge or port change that my neighbour heard near the bakery. They had no clear source, and the secretary has heard of no actual proposal or announcement. I do not know whether any change is intended or what its purpose might be. I have asked the secretary to check discreetly for a firsthand source or submitted proposal without spreading the rumour as fact.

The innkeeper requested a community gathering tomorrow at eighteen hundred in the great hall. I approved it, and the secretary says it is recorded with the appointments. The innkeeper also wanted to discuss catering privately with the secretary; that appears connected to arranging the gathering, and I have no evidence of another purpose.

The accounts review remains unfinished because neither the secretary nor I has located a ledger. The treasury chest contained 128 emeralds but no ledger. The secretary has now asked where correspondence is normally deposited and who last maintained the ledger; I do not presently know either answer. That is an administrative gap, not evidence of wrongdoing. I am still in the office and am scheduled to return home at nineteen hundred.
